alt.en: A printed book page with no music. Under the heading "LXXXIV." are seven lines beginning "O that I had wings like a dove!"; under "LXXXV." come the first two verses of "Nearer, my God, to thee", the first ending "Still all my song would be, Nearer, my God, to thee, Nearer to thee!" and the second beginning "Though like the wanderer, The sun gone down".
alt.es: Una página de libro impresa, sin música. Bajo el encabezado "LXXXIV." hay siete versos que empiezan "O that I had wings like a dove!"; bajo "LXXXV." vienen las dos primeras estrofas de "Nearer, my God, to thee": la primera termina "Still all my song would be, Nearer, my God, to thee, Nearer to thee!" y la segunda empieza "Though like the wanderer, The sun gone down".

caption.en: No. 85 in William Johnson Fox's Hymns and Anthems (London, 1841), the hymn's earliest known printing, words only, with Adams's own "Still all my song would be" in the first verse.
caption.es: El n.º 85 de Hymns and Anthems, de William Johnson Fox (Londres, 1841), la primera impresión conocida del himno, solo con la letra y con el "Still all my song would be" de la propia Adams en la primera estrofa.

source: Hymns and Anthems (London: Charles Fox, 1841), No. LXXXV, "Nearer, my God, to thee" (with the end of No. LXXXIV above it); scan page n70
library: New York Public Library (digitized by Google; Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1841; Sarah Flower Adams died 1848, William Johnson Fox 1864. IA record: "possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT". Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: New York Public Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A handwritten page reproduced in black on white: the first three verses of "Nearer my God to thee" in a slanting hand, each followed by a line marked "Response." with "Nearer my God to thee, Nearer to thee" and a short double stroke between verses. In the second and third verses a few words are corrected above and below the line.
alt.es: Una página manuscrita reproducida en negro sobre blanco: las tres primeras estrofas de "Nearer my God to thee" en letra inclinada, cada una seguida de un verso marcado "Response." con "Nearer my God to thee, Nearer to thee" y una doble raya corta entre estrofas. En la segunda y la tercera estrofa hay algunas palabras corregidas por encima y por debajo del renglón.

caption.en: Sarah Flower Adams's draft of the hymn, sent to Fox and dated November 1840 on its second page, as Moncure Conway reproduced it in 1894, laid out for choir and congregation to answer each other, with a "Response" after each verse.
caption.es: El borrador del himno de Sarah Flower Adams, enviado a Fox y fechado en noviembre de 1840 en su segunda página, tal como lo reprodujo Moncure Conway en 1894, dispuesto para que el coro y la congregación se respondieran, con una "Response" (respuesta) tras cada estrofa.

source: Moncure D. Conway, Centenary History of the South Place Society (London: Williams and Norgate, 1894), plate "Manuscript of 'Nearer, my God, to Thee'. From the Original Draft of the Hymn sent by the Author to Mr. Fox", first page; scan page n77
library: Cornell University Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Cornell University Library BX9934 .C76; Internet Archive cu31924029481342
licenceEvidence: Draft written 1840 by Sarah Flower Adams (died 1848), published in facsimile 1894 by Moncure D. Conway (1832-1907). The scan's own front leaf: "There are no known copyright restrictions in the United States on the use of the text." Faithful reproduction of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Cornell University Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A yellowed page numbered 244, headed "THE SABBATH HYMN AND TUNE BOOK." At the top, "BETHANY. 6s & 4s." in four parts on three systems of treble and bass staves, with no words under the notes. Below, hymn 989, "Nearer, my God, to Thee", in five numbered verses, with repeat signs around each verse's sixth line, and beside it hymn 1224, "I'm but a stranger here, Heaven is my home".
alt.es: Una página amarillenta numerada 244, con el encabezado "THE SABBATH HYMN AND TUNE BOOK." Arriba, "BETHANY. 6s & 4s." a cuatro voces en tres sistemas de pentagramas en clave de sol y de fa, sin letra bajo las notas. Debajo, el himno 989, "Nearer, my God, to Thee", en cinco estrofas numeradas, con signos de repetición alrededor del sexto verso de cada estrofa, y a su lado el himno 1224, "I'm but a stranger here, Heaven is my home".

caption.en: Page 244 of The Sabbath Hymn and Tune Book (New York, 1859), the earliest known printing of Lowell Mason's BETHANY with these words, and the four parts our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: La página 244 de The Sabbath Hymn and Tune Book (Nueva York, 1859), la primera impresión conocida de BETHANY, de Lowell Mason, con esta letra, y las cuatro voces de las que está tomado nuestro arreglo.

source: The Sabbath Hymn and Tune Book, for the Service of Song in the House of the Lord, ed. Lowell Mason, Edwards A. Park and Austin Phelps (New York: Mason Brothers, 1859), p. 244, BETHANY and hymn 989; scan page n249
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Princeton Theological Seminary Library SCC; Internet Archive sabbtune00maso
licenceEvidence: Printed New York 1859; Mason died 1872, Park 1900, Phelps 1890, Adams 1848; hymn 1224 by Thomas R. Taylor, died 1835. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A cream book page with no page number. At the top, in quotation marks, "Whom have I in heaven but Thee, and there is none upon earth that I desire in comparison of Thee." Below are four verses of "Nearer, my God, to Thee", opening with a large capital N, including "Darkness comes over me" and "There let my way appear"; at the foot a short "A-men." in treble and bass staves.
alt.es: Una página de libro color crema, sin número de página. Arriba, entre comillas, "Whom have I in heaven but Thee, and there is none upon earth that I desire in comparison of Thee." Debajo, cuatro estrofas de "Nearer, my God, to Thee", que empiezan con una N mayúscula grande, entre ellas "Darkness comes over me" y "There let my way appear"; al pie, un breve "A-men." en pentagramas en clave de sol y de fa.

caption.en: Hymn 200 in Hymns Ancient and Modern (London, 1861), the Church of England's book: four of Adams's five verses, with its own changes, among them "Darkness comes over me" and "There let my way appear".
caption.es: El himno 200 de Hymns Ancient and Modern (Londres, 1861), el libro de la Iglesia de Inglaterra: cuatro de las cinco estrofas de Adams, con sus propios cambios, entre ellos "Darkness comes over me" y "There let my way appear".

source: Hymns Ancient and Modern, for use in the services of the Church, with accompanying tunes, musical editor William Henry Monk (London: Novello, 1861), Hymn 200, words page; scan page n280
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
